chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'at, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who passes by a funeral while he is without ablution, what should he do? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should strike with his hands upon a brick wall and perform Tayammum with it.'
ai.seo_question: How to perform Tayammum for funeral prayer when without water or wudu?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the practical flexibility of Shia jurisprudence regarding ritual purity, specifically validating Tayammum against a 'brick wall' (hā'it al-labn) as a valid substitute for water when time is short or water is unavailable. It underscores the importance of maintaining communal religious duties, such as praying the Janazah, even in states of minor impurity, by utilizing the easiest available means of purification.
